description:
Make the lease check inside repository mutations hold one lease lock across the session and read its targets through it, without writing and without locking twice.

## Background

The repository-mutation guard `lock_claims_for_repository_mutation` (`crates/jit/src/storage/claim_coordinator.rs:413-432`) takes the claims lock and replays the whole claims log into a snapshot. `claims_mutation_guard` (`commands/mod.rs:720-739`) takes it before the repository session opens (`commands/mod.rs:2600-2607`), and `captured_lease_warnings` and `ensure_claim_available` (`commands/mod.rs:741-800`) read the snapshot. `CoordinationOrderGuard::enter` refuses while a repository order guard is held (`storage/guard_order.rs:52-62`). `ClaimCoordinator::lock()` returns a `LeaseLock` with `load`, `list` and `apply`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The repository-mutation guard takes one `LeaseLock` before the repository session opens, holds it across the session and reads each target only through `load`; it writes nothing, takes no second claims lock and enters no second coordination guard, and an expired lease counts as inactive.
- [hard] REQ-02: A test shows that a lease-enforced mutation succeeds for the lease holder, is refused for another agent, and leaves the claims log unchanged.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the semantic-types epic (2195c98f): issue ids are `IssueId`, gate-run ids `GateRunId`, gate keys `GateKey`, lease ids `LeaseId`, events are an `Event` envelope around a tagged `EventBody`, and record paths come from `VirtualPath` constructors. Line citations name current code, which that epic retypes.
title: The repository-mutation lease check reads through the held lease lock
